study: Heller et al. 2012 (JRST), WestEd Making Sense of SCIENCE PD (electric circuits) [same trial as heller_2010]
eval_evidence: Journal version of the same RCT; conducted by WestEd, the developers of the Making Sense of SCIENCE / Learning Science for Teaching courses (authors are WestEd staff). NSF-funded but developer-conducted.
developer_evidence: 'Interventions were delivered by staff developers trained to lead the teacher courses in their regions'; 'courses implemented by local facilitators trained at WestEd', with two local facilitators per site co-delivering each course (San Francisco Bay Area excepted, where WestEd developers were solo facilitators).
cascade_evidence: WestEd trained local facilitators at WestEd in Oakland; those facilitators then delivered the courses to teachers in their regions: developer -> trained local facilitator -> teacher (>=1 hop).
counterfactual_evidence: Three PD arms vs a shared no-treatment control; control teachers received no course (offered it the following summer). Business-as-usual.
coaching_evidence: Each course comprised eight three-hour facilitated sessions (content + pedagogy-analysis components) over weeks; a course/workshop format, no recurring in-class coaching cycles in teachers' own classrooms.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention builds teacher content/pedagogical-content knowledge for the existing electric-circuits unit; only the teacher's regular instruction changes, no added student-facing dose.
maturity_evidence: Single-year PD course; the primary (study-year) student content-knowledge outcome is the immediate post-intervention gain. No maturity axis for the core contrast (a separate follow-up-year cohort exists but is a different student sample).
